title: Exposure to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs during pregnancy and the risk of selected birth defects: a prospective cohort study.
ehr_evidence: To obtain information on pregnancy outcome, data from MoBa were linked to records in the Medical Birth Registry of Norway (MBRN) using the women's personal identification number.
summary: In this prospective cohort study of 67,891 Norwegian pregnant women, NSAID use during the first 12 weeks of gestation was not associated with an increased risk of selected birth defects.
key_findings: No association between any NSAID use during gestational weeks 0-12 and all selected birth defects as a group (adjusted OR 0.7, 95% CI 0.4-1.1).

No association with any individual birth defect category, including congenital heart defects (adjusted OR 0.9, 95% CI 0.5-1.4), septal defects (adjusted OR 0.8, 95% CI 0.5-1.4), ventricular septal defects (adjusted OR 0.7, 95% CI 0.4-1.4), and atrial septal defects (adjusted OR 1.1, 95% CI 0.5-2.3).
A non-statistically significant increased risk for septal defects after exposure to multiple NSAIDs based on only 2 exposed cases (crude OR 3.9, 95% CI 0.9-15.7).
captured_features: Maternal NSAID use (type, timing, and exposure window 0-12 weeks of gestation)
Birth defect diagnosis coded by ICD-10
History of miscarriages, stillbirths, or induced abortions
pathologies_diseases: Congenital heart defects (conotruncal, septal, ventricular septal, atrial septal)
data_source_type: Registry (Medical Birth Registry of Norway) linked to prospective cohort questionnaire data
population: 67,891 pregnant women from the Norwegian Mother and Child Cohort Study (MoBa), enrolled 1999-2006, living in Norway; maternal age at delivery ranged from <20 to ≥40 years.
exposure_domain: Medication (non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug) use during pregnancy
limitations: Small number of NSAID-exposed infants for individual birth defect categories, requiring lumping of defects and reducing power.
Self-administered questionnaire exposure assessment with potential non-differential misclassification and inability to separate occasional from frequent users.
Relatively low participation rate (43.5%) with potential selection bias.
Outcome misclassification because cardiovascular malformations in the registry were not validated by geneticist/dysmorphologist.
Confounding by indication could not be completely excluded.
